sourceSummary: Email and password sign-in for registered customers, with lockout after repeated failures and an optional 30-day session.

testCases.title: Valid credentials sign the customer in and land them on the account page
preconditions: A registered customer exists with a known password

steps.expectedObservation: The Email field, Password field and Sign in button are visible

testCases.expectedResult: The customer is on /account and their name is visible in the header.
testCases.rationale: The primary path. If this breaks, every other case is untestable.

testCases.title: Remember me extends the session to 30 days
preconditions: A registered customer exists with a known password
testCases.expectedResult: The session cookie expires roughly 30 days out rather than 24 hours.
testCases.rationale: Catches the common wiring bug where the checkbox is read but the cookie max-age is left at the default.

testCases.title: Wrong password shows the error and keeps the customer on the page
preconditions: A registered customer exists with a known password

steps.expectedObservation: An error message appears above the form

testCases.expectedResult: The message "Email or password is incorrect" is shown and the URL is still /sign-in.
testCases.rationale: Catches both the missing-error-message bug and the redirect-anyway bug, which are different failures with the same symptom to a user.

testCases.title: Unregistered email produces the same error as a wrong password
testCases.expectedResult: The error text is identical to the wrong-password error, with no indication that the account does not exist.
testCases.rationale: Catches user enumeration: a distinct "no such account" message lets an attacker harvest valid customer emails.

testCases.title: Submitting with both fields empty does not attempt a sign-in

steps.action: Click the "Sign in" button without typing anything
steps.expectedObservation: Validation messages appear on both fields

testCases.expectedResult: Both fields are marked as required and no network request to the sign-in endpoint is made.
testCases.rationale: Catches the case where an empty submission counts toward the 5-attempt lockout, letting anyone lock out any account.

testCases.title: A 7-character password is rejected and an 8-character one is accepted
preconditions: A registered customer exists whose password is exactly 8 characters

steps.action: Type a 7-character password into the Password field
Replace the password with the correct 8-character password

testCases.expectedResult: 7 characters is rejected client-side; exactly 8 characters signs in successfully.
testCases.rationale: Catches the off-by-one where the minimum is implemented as > 8 rather than >= 8, locking out every customer sitting exactly on the limit.

testCases.title: A 65-character password is rejected while 64 characters is accepted
preconditions: A registered customer exists whose password is exactly 64 characters

steps.action: Type a 65-character password into the Password field
steps.expectedObservation: The field either refuses the 65th character or shows a validation message

steps.action: Replace it with the correct 64-character password and click "Sign in"

testCases.expectedResult: 64 characters signs in; 65 is refused rather than silently truncated.
testCases.rationale: Catches silent truncation at the upper bound, where a 65-character password is accepted at sign-up but stored as 64 and can then be signed in with either.

testCases.title: The sixth consecutive failed attempt is blocked rather than merely rejected
preconditions: No failed attempts have been recorded for this email in the last 15 minutes

steps.action: Submit the form five times with "ada@example.com" and a wrong password
steps.expectedObservation: Each attempt shows the incorrect-credentials error

steps.action: Submit a sixth time with the CORRECT password
steps.expectedObservation: A lockout message appears instead of a successful sign-in

testCases.expectedResult: The sixth attempt is blocked with a lockout message and does not sign the customer in, even though the credentials are valid.
testCases.rationale: Catches the lockout that counts attempts but never enforces them — the check is easy to write and easy to leave unwired, and it only fails on the sixth request.

testCases.title: Trailing whitespace in the email does not prevent sign-in
preconditions: A registered customer exists with a known password

steps.action: Type "ada@example.com " (with a trailing space) into the Email field

testCases.expectedResult: The email is trimmed before lookup and sign-in succeeds.
testCases.rationale: Catches the support-ticket generator where a password manager or mobile keyboard appends a space and the customer is told their password is wrong.

testCases.title: The password never appears in the URL or in plain text

steps.action: Read the type attribute of the Password field
steps.expectedObservation: It is "password", so the value is masked

steps.action: Type "Correct-Horse-9" into the Password field and click "Sign in"
Read the full URL after navigation

testCases.expectedResult: The password does not appear in the URL, and the field is masked at all times.
testCases.rationale: Catches a form defaulting to GET, which puts the password in the address bar, browser history, and every downstream referer header.
